Unleash Enterprise Pay-As-You-Go costs $75 per seat per month, billed monthly by credit card, with no contract. A seat is a user of Unleash, not a user of your application. You can start a 14-day trial with no credit card required.
Unleash Open Source is free and has no seat limit. Enterprise annual contracts are quoted per customer and invoiced.
Is there a free version of Unleash?

Yes. Unleash Open Source is free, self-hosted, and has no limit on seats. It covers the core feature set, with a limit of 1 project, 2 environments, and 5,000 feature flags per instance. Thousands of teams run it in production.

It does not include single sign-on, SCIM provisioning, granular role-based access control, change request approvals, or a support SLA. If you need those, or you would rather not operate the service yourself, Pay-As-You-Go starts at $75 per seat per month with a 14-day free trial.
Why does Unleash charge per seat?
Because per-seat pricing is predictable, and usage-based pricing works against how feature flags should be used.

You can forecast a seat-based bill from your headcount. A usage-based bill moves with your production traffic, which is the thing you have least control over. Usage pricing also creates a cost incentive to use fewer flags, and we think the opposite behaviour is correct: every code change should be able to sit behind a flag. Metering evaluations would penalize that.
Your bill does not change when your application’s traffic grows.
Does Unleash charge for flag evaluations or monthly active users?
No. Client-side monthly active users are unlimited on every paid plan, and flag evaluations are never billed.

Unleash backend SDKs fetch the flag configuration once, cache it in memory, and evaluate flags locally. A service can evaluate a flag a million times per second without generating a single additional request to Unleash. This is also why no end-user data leaves your infrastructure when you use server-side SDKs.
What is included in the 53 million API requests, and what happens if I go over?
The Pay-As-You-Go plan on Unleash Cloud includes 53 million API requests per month. Additional requests are billed at $5 per million.

Requests come from your SDKs synchronizing with Unleash, not from your end users. As an example, 200 backend service instances polling at the 15-second default generate roughly 34.6 million requests per month, inside the included allowance.
If you need more, Unleash Edge absorbs SDK traffic and reduces upstream requests, and Enterprise contracts can include a higher allowance.
What is the difference between Pay-As-You-Go and Enterprise?
Both give you the full Enterprise feature set. The differences are commercial and operational.

Pay-As-You-Go is self-service: $75 per seat per month, monthly credit card billing, no contract, standard support with a one business day response target, and a 99.9% uptime commitment. Best for teams that want to start immediately without procurement.

Enterprise is an annual contract, invoiced, with a 99.99% uptime commitment, response times tiered by severity, access to customer success, and optional add-ons including private instances, multi-region Edge, access logs, IP restrictions, and US or EU data residency. Best for organizations with procurement, compliance, or scale requirements.
Is Unleash cheaper than building feature flags ourselves?
Usually, and the gap widens over time. The build cost is rarely the problem. Maintenance can account for more than 90% of a homegrown solution’s total cost of ownership.

For example, Wayfair migrated more than 15,000 feature flags and 1,000 developers onto Unleash, replacing an in-house system that had contributed to holiday-season downtime at $3.4 million per hour. They
estimate Unleash Enterprise costs about a third of what their homegrown solution did.
